## formal
Scalars of family matrices are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, $^{*}$ is $I_{4} \mapsto -I_{4}$ on entries, $^{\dagger}$ its composite with the transpose, and a \emph{unit} is $z = e^{I_{4}\gamma}$, as in Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jarlskog-commutator-identity}. On a charge-preserving point of the rung field, with rung-$4$ components $\alpha$, $\beta$ and family matrices $Y$, $\tilde{Y}$ of size $N \times N$, the covariant completion (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix}; in the chart of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-left-right-bidoublet-two-yukawa-couplings}) has
\[
M_{u} = \alpha Y + \bar{\beta}\tilde{Y}, \qquad M_{d} = \beta Y + \bar{\alpha}\tilde{Y}, \qquad m(c) = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2}) .
\]
Let $H_{q} = M_{q}M_{q}^{\dagger}$, $D = \det[H_{u}, H_{d}]$ and
\[
\Theta = \det M_{u}\,\det M_{d} = |\Theta|\,e^{I_{4}\theta_{M}} ,
\]
so that $\theta_{M}$ is the phase of the determinant of the quark mass matrices, the \emph{mass phase}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The completion does not constrain the pair.)} If $m(c) \neq 0$, the map $(Y, \tilde{Y}) \mapsto (M_{u}, M_{d})$ is a bijection of pairs of $N \times N$ matrices, with inverse
\[
Y = \frac{\bar{\alpha}M_{u} - \bar{\beta}M_{d}}{2m(c)}, \qquad \tilde{Y} = \frac{\alpha M_{d} - \beta M_{u}}{2m(c)},
\]
and it maps pairs of symmetric matrices onto pairs of symmetric matrices. Hence for every unit $z$ the pair $(zM_{u}, M_{d})$ is realised at the same point of the rung field by family matrices of the same kind; it has the same $H_{u}$, $H_{d}$, so the same masses, the same mixing matrix and the same $D$, and $\Theta$ is multiplied by $z^{N}$. So $\theta_{M}$ is a function of the stored data $(\alpha, \beta, Y, \tilde{Y})$, namely the phase of $\det(\alpha Y + \bar{\beta}\tilde{Y})\det(\beta Y + \bar{\alpha}\tilde{Y})$, that takes every value at fixed masses and mixing: no stored statement about masses and mixing fixes it. On the balanced frame, $m(c) = 0$, $M_{d} = (\beta/\alpha)M_{u}$, $D = 0$ and $\Theta = (\beta/\alpha)^{N}(\det M_{u})^{2}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(What moves it.)} $\Theta$ is unchanged by the hypercharge phase $\alpha \mapsto z\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto \bar{z}\beta$ of the rung field, and is changed by the common phase $\alpha, \beta \mapsto z\alpha, z\beta$ at fixed family matrices. The exchange $(Y, \tilde{Y}) \mapsto (\tilde{Y}^{*}, Y^{*})$ sends $(M_{u}, M_{d})$ to $(M_{d}^{*}, M_{u}^{*})$ and $\Theta$ to $\Theta^{*}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Three readings with a real determinant, and what each costs.)} (a) \emph{Real.} If $\alpha$, $\beta$, $Y$, $\tilde{Y}$ are real, $\Theta$ is real, of either sign, and $D = 0$: by the cited Fact the Jarlskog invariant vanishes. (b) \emph{Self-conjugate coupling.} If $\tilde{Y} = Y^{*}$, the coupling $Yc + \tilde{Y}c^{*}$ being fixed by the conjugation, then in every frame $M_{d} = M_{u}^{*}$, $\Theta = |\det M_{u}|^{2} \ge 0$, so $\theta_{M} = 0$, and $D \neq 0$ generically; but $H_{d} = H_{u}^{*}$, so the up and down mass spectra are equal. (c) \emph{Hermitian.} If $Y$ and $\tilde{Y}$ are Hermitian and $\alpha$, $\beta$ real, then $M_{u}$, $M_{d}$ are Hermitian, $\Theta$ is real, $D \neq 0$ generically and the spectra are unequal: the parity mechanism of left-right models. A matrix that is Hermitian and symmetric is real, so for the symmetric family matrices of a $10$ this reading is (a).
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Stages.)} Let $M_{q} = c_{q}\bigl(\J + \delta_{q}(E + X_{q})\bigr)$, $q = u, d$, with $\J$ the matrix of ones, $E = e_{3}e_{3}^{\mathsf{T}}$ and $X_{q}$ odd under the exchange $P_{12}$ of the first two families, the textures of \claimref{synthesis.cabibbo-from-one-type-quark-stages-selects-near-quarter-turn-phase}. An odd $X$ has entries $X_{11} = -X_{22} = p$, $X_{12} = -X_{21} = q$, $X_{13} = -X_{23} = r$, $X_{31} = -X_{32} = s$, and exactly
\[
\det\bigl(\J + \delta(E + X)\bigr) = -3\delta^{2}xy + \delta^{3}(q^{2} - p^{2}), \qquad xy = \tfrac13(p - q - 2s)(p + q - 2r),
\]
with $x$, $y$ the off-diagonal entries of the light-plane block $\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} 2/3 & x \\ y & 0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ of \claimref{synthesis.solar-angle-light-plane-sum-rule}(i). For one-type symmetric stages $X_{q} = t_{q}S_{q}$, $S_{q}$ real symmetric with entries $p_{q}$, $r_{q}$, and $c_{q}$, $\delta_{q} > 0$ real,
\[
\Theta = (c_{u}c_{d})^{3}(\delta_{u}\delta_{d})^{2}\,(t_{u}t_{d})^{2}\,R, \qquad R = \prod_{q}\bigl((p_{q} - 2r_{q})^{2} + \delta_{q}p_{q}^{2}\bigr) > 0 .
\]
So $\theta_{M} = 2(\arg t_{u} + \arg t_{d})$, plus a half turn if $c_{u}c_{d} < 0$, while the up-down phase $\phi$ of the cited result is $\pm(\arg t_{u} - \arg t_{d})$ modulo a half turn: the two are independent. If one coefficient is real, $\Theta$ is $\operatorname{sgn}(c_{u}c_{d})\,e^{\pm2I_{4}\phi}$ times a positive number, so $\cos\theta_{M} = \operatorname{sgn}(c_{u}c_{d})(2\cos^{2}\phi - 1)$ and
\[
\Theta \text{ is real} \iff \cos\phi \in \{0, \pm1\} .
\]
The cited result excludes $\cos\phi = \pm1$ and selects $|\cos\phi| < \tfrac12$; on that range $|\cos\theta_{M}| > \tfrac12$, the mass phase is within a sixth of a turn of $0$ or of a half turn, and it is $0$ or a half turn exactly at the quarter turn $\cos\phi = 0$: $\theta_{M} = 0$ for $c_{u}c_{d} < 0$ and a half turn for $c_{u}c_{d} > 0$. At the quarter turn, with $t_{d}$ real and $t_{u} = I_{4}\tau$, $\tau$ real: $M_{d}^{*} = M_{d}$ and $P_{12}M_{u}^{*}P_{12} = M_{u}$, the up matrix is the twin $M_{h}P_{12}$ of a Hermitian matrix $M_{h}$ in the sense of \claimref{synthesis.one-type-second-stages-are-twins}, $D \neq 0$ generically and the spectra are unequal. With both coefficients real, or both a quarter turn, one conjugation fixes both matrices and $D = 0$, as \claimref{synthesis.flag-conjugate-antilinear-on-one-chirality-and-conjugation-reverses-jarlskog}(iii) requires. Two complex coefficients give a real $\Theta$ when $\arg t_{u} + \arg t_{d}$ is a multiple of a quarter turn, for instance opposite eighth turns.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading (argued).} The series does not fix the mass phase. By (i) the stored completion leaves the pair of quark mass matrices as free as two arbitrary symmetric matrices, so nothing short of an added premise on $Y$, $\tilde{Y}$ and the frame can fix $\theta_{M}$. Of the premises in the store: the adjoint reading of the action clause of \claimref{dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance} is satisfied by every $(Y, \tilde{Y})$ and constrains nothing; the real-breaking assumption (\claimref{neutrino.real-breaking-assumption}), stated for the lepton matrices, would if extended to the quark matrices be reading (a), which the store's nonzero Jarlskog invariant and its exclusion of $\cos\phi = \pm1$ close; reading (b) is closed by the top and bottom masses; reading (c) is not available for symmetric family matrices. What stays open is the reading of (iv): a real vacuum with real first stages in both sectors, a real second stage in one sector and a second stage at an exact quarter turn in the other. On it the determinant is real with a nonzero Jarlskog invariant, and the stored Cabibbo relation holds with no free phase, $|V_{us}|^{2} = (x + y)/((1 + x)(1 + y))$, which the stored windows of the mass ratios allow and do not yet test. That is half a result in the sense of the open problem, and it is less than it looks: it is a property of a texture at tree level, the two sectors being fixed by two different conjugations, which is not a symmetry of the coupled theory (a common one gives $D = 0$), so nothing stored protects it against corrections; its sign, zero angle or half turn, is the sign of $-c_{u}c_{d}$, which nothing stored fixes; and it says nothing about the coefficient of the colour four-form, to which $\theta_{M}$ is only added. A physical angle below $10^{-10}$ would need on this reading, besides a vanishing coefficient, $|\cos\phi|$ of the same order, that is, a reason for the exact quarter turn.

## technical
The stored quark masses come from two family matrices and two components of the rung field. Solving for the family matrices shows that, away from the balanced frame, every pair of mass matrices arises from exactly one pair of family matrices. The structure therefore fixes nothing about the pair, and in particular one may turn the up matrix by any phase without changing a single mass or mixing angle while the determinant's phase turns freely. The phase of the determinant, which adds to the strong CP angle, is a free number of the stored structure.

The determinant is real on four readings. Real matrices: but then there is no CP violation in the quark mixing, against the data and against the store's own Cabibbo result. A coupling equal to its own conjugate: then the up and down quarks have equal masses. Hermitian matrices, the classical left-right solution: but the family matrices of a $10$ are symmetric, and symmetric Hermitian matrices are real. The fourth survives: with the democratic textures the store uses, the determinant of a sector is an explicit square of its second-stage coefficient, so the determinant's phase is twice the sum of the two sectors' phases while the Cabibbo phase is their difference. If one sector is real, the determinant is real exactly when the Cabibbo phase is a quarter turn, the value the data select. The up matrix is then a Hermitian matrix composed with the exchange of the first two families.

This does not solve the strong CP problem: the bare angle is untouched, the sign (zero or a half turn) is open, and the pattern is not a symmetry, so loop corrections are not controlled.

## lay
One number of particle physics, the strong CP angle, is measured to be zero to ten decimal places, and no one knows why. Part of it comes from the quark masses: a phase attached to the product of all of them. This result asks whether the series' description of quark masses fixes that phase. It does not: the description is exactly as flexible as the Standard Model's. There is one suggestive pattern. If all the ingredients are real except one, and that one is turned by exactly a quarter turn, the phase vanishes or equals a half turn, and the quarter turn is the value that the measured mixing of the first two quark families already asks for. But the pattern is not enforced by any symmetry of the series, and it leaves the other part of the angle untouched.

## one-liner
For $m(c) \neq 0$ the covariant completion $(Y, \tilde{Y}) \mapsto (M_{u}, M_{d})$ is a bijection, so the phase $\theta_{M}$ of $\det M_{u}\det M_{d}$ is free at fixed masses and mixing; it vanishes for real matrices ($D = 0$), for $\tilde{Y} = Y^{*}$ (equal up and down spectra) and for Hermitian matrices (real when symmetric); on one-type symmetric stages $\Theta = (c_{u}c_{d})^{3}(\delta_{u}\delta_{d})^{2}(t_{u}t_{d})^{2}R$, $R > 0$, so with one sector real $\Theta$ is real exactly when the stored up-down phase is a quarter turn ($D \neq 0$, sign $-\operatorname{sgn}(c_{u}c_{d})$): a tree-level texture, not a symmetry, and silent on the bare angle.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{(i).} The pair $(M_{u}, M_{d})$ is obtained from $(Y, \tilde{Y})$ by the $2 \times 2$ array of scalars $\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}\alpha & \bar{\beta} \\ \beta & \bar{\alpha}\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix}; the same formulas in the chart of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-left-right-bidoublet-two-yukawa-couplings}), whose determinant is $|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2} = 2m(c)$. For $m(c) \neq 0$ its inverse gives the stated formulas: $\bar{\alpha}M_{u} - \bar{\beta}M_{d} = (|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2})Y$ and $\alpha M_{d} - \beta M_{u} = (|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2})\tilde{Y}$. The map and its inverse are linear combinations with scalar coefficients, so they preserve symmetry of the matrices. Given $(M_{u}, M_{d})$ and a unit $z$, the pair $(zM_{u}, M_{d})$ has $H_{u}' = z\bar{z}H_{u} = H_{u}$ and $H_{d}' = H_{d}$; the masses are the square roots of the eigenvalues of $H_{q}$, the mixing matrix is built from their eigenvectors, and $D$ is a function of $H_{u}$, $H_{d}$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-jarlskog-commutator-identity}); $\det(zM_{u}) = z^{N}\det M_{u}$. As $z$ runs over the units $z^{N}$ runs over all of them. If $|\alpha| = |\beta|$ then $\bar{\alpha} = |\beta|^{2}/\alpha$, so $M_{d} = (\beta/\alpha)(\alpha Y + \bar{\beta}\tilde{Y}) = (\beta/\alpha)M_{u}$, $H_{d} = H_{u}$ and $D = 0$. The check verifies the inverse on a real and a non-real frame with symmetric samples, the turn by $z = \tfrac15(3 + 4I_{4})$ with $z^{3} = \tfrac{1}{125}(-117 + 44I_{4})$, and the balanced frame $\alpha = 3 + 4I_{4}$, $\beta = 5I_{4}$.

\emph{(ii).} Under $\alpha \mapsto z\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto \bar{z}\beta$: $M_{u} \mapsto zM_{u}$, $M_{d} \mapsto \bar{z}M_{d}$ and $\Theta \mapsto (z\bar{z})^{N}\Theta = \Theta$. Under the common phase the two terms of each $M_{q}$ turn oppositely, and $\Theta$ changes for generic matrices (checked on the sample). Under the exchange, $M_{u} \mapsto \alpha\tilde{Y}^{*} + \bar{\beta}Y^{*} = (\bar{\alpha}\tilde{Y} + \beta Y)^{*} = M_{d}^{*}$ and likewise $M_{d} \mapsto M_{u}^{*}$.

\emph{(iii).} (a) Real matrices have a real determinant, and real $M_{q}$ give real symmetric $H_{q}$, for which $D = 0$ (\claimref{synthesis.flag-conjugate-antilinear-on-one-chirality-and-conjugation-reverses-jarlskog}(iii)); changing the sign of $\tilde{Y}$ in the sample changes the sign of $\Theta$. (b) By (ii) with $\tilde{Y} = Y^{*}$ the pair is fixed by the exchange, so $M_{d} = M_{u}^{*}$, $\det M_{d} = (\det M_{u})^{*}$ and $\Theta = |\det M_{u}|^{2}$; $H_{d} = H_{u}^{*} = H_{u}^{\mathsf{T}}$ has the characteristic polynomial of $H_{u}$. With $H_{u} = A + I_{4}B$, $A$ real symmetric and $B$ real antisymmetric, $[H_{u}, H_{u}^{*}] = -2I_{4}[A, B]$ and $D = 8I_{4}\det[A, B]$ for $N = 3$, not zero in general; the sample has $D = 10909000000\,I_{4}$. (c) A real combination of Hermitian matrices is Hermitian and has a real determinant; the sample has $D \neq 0$ and different characteristic polynomials of $H_{u}$, $H_{d}$, and with a non-real frame $\Theta$ is not real. If $M = M^{\dagger} = M^{\mathsf{T}}$ then $M^{*} = M$.

\emph{(iv).} The condition $P_{12}XP_{12} = -X$ exchanges the indices $1$ and $2$ and changes the sign, which gives the four entries $p, q, r, s$ and $X_{33} = 0$. With $A = E + X$, $\det(\J + \delta A) = \delta^{3}\det A + \delta^{2}\sum_{ab}\mathrm{cof}(A)_{ab}$, the terms of order $\delta$ and $1$ vanishing because $\J$ has rank one. Expanding, $\det A = q^{2} - p^{2}$ and $\sum_{ab}\mathrm{cof}(A)_{ab} = q^{2} - p^{2} + 2r(p - q) + 2s(p + q) - 4rs = -(p - q - 2s)(p + q - 2r)$. In the basis $\hat{b}_{e} = (1, 1, -2)/\sqrt6$, $\hat{b}_{o} = (1, -1, 0)/\sqrt2$ of the cited sum rule, $x = \hat{b}_{e}^{\mathsf{T}}X\hat{b}_{o} = (p - q - 2s)/\sqrt3$ and $y = \hat{b}_{o}^{\mathsf{T}}X\hat{b}_{e} = (p + q - 2r)/\sqrt3$, so the sum of cofactors is $-3xy$: three times the determinant $-xy$ of the light-plane block (\claimref{synthesis.solar-angle-light-plane-sum-rule}(i)). The check verifies the formula on three samples with entries in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$. For a symmetric one-type stage, $q = 0$, $s = r$ and the entries are $t$ times real numbers: $\det = -\delta^{2}t^{2}\bigl((p - 2r)^{2} + \delta p^{2}\bigr)$, and $\det M_{q} = c_{q}^{3}$ times it. The product over the two sectors gives $\Theta$, the two signs cancelling. The off-diagonal entry of $B_{q}B_{q}^{\dagger}$ is $\tfrac23\bar{y}_{q} = \tfrac23\bar{t}_{q}(p_{q} - 2r_{q})/\sqrt3$, so the relative phase $\phi$ of \claimref{synthesis.cabibbo-from-one-type-quark-stages-selects-near-quarter-turn-phase} is $\pm(\arg t_{u} - \arg t_{d})$ up to a half turn from the signs of the real factors; $e^{2I_{4}\phi}$ is unaffected by the half turn. If $t_{d}$ is real, $(t_{u}t_{d})^{2}$ is a positive number times $e^{\pm2I_{4}\phi}$, which is real exactly when $\sin2\phi = 0$; $\cos2\phi = 2\cos^{2}\phi - 1 < -\tfrac12$ when $\cos^{2}\phi < \tfrac14$. At the quarter turn $(t_{u}t_{d})^{2} < 0$, so $\Theta$ has the sign of $-c_{u}c_{d}$. With $t_{u} = I_{4}\tau$: $M_{u} = c_{u}(\J + \delta_{u}E) + I_{4}c_{u}\delta_{u}\tau S_{u}$, the first part even and the second odd under $P_{12}$, both real, so $P_{12}M_{u}^{*}P_{12} = M_{u}$; and $(M_{u}P_{12})^{\dagger} = P_{12}M_{u}^{*} = M_{u}P_{12}$, using that $M_{u}$ is symmetric: $M_{h} = M_{u}P_{12}$ is Hermitian and $M_{u} = M_{h}P_{12}$, the twin relation of \claimref{synthesis.one-type-second-stages-are-twins}, with $\det M_{u} = -\det M_{h}$. If one antiunitary conjugation $M \mapsto PM^{*}P$ with a real orthogonal $P$ fixes both matrices, then $H_{q} = PH_{q}^{*}P$ for both and $D = \det[H_{u}^{*}, H_{d}^{*}] = -D$ by clause (iii) of the result on the flag conjugate, so $D = 0$: with both coefficients real $P = 1$, with both at a quarter turn $P = P_{12}$. The check verifies on a sample with $t_{u} = 2I_{4}$, $t_{d} = 3$: $\Theta$ real and negative for $c_{u}c_{d} > 0$, positive for $c_{u}c_{d} < 0$, $D \neq 0$, different characteristic polynomials, the two conjugation properties and the Hermitian twin; that an eighth turn against a real coefficient gives a non-real $\Theta$ and opposite eighth turns a positive one; and that $\Theta/(t_{u}t_{d})^{2}$ is real with the sign of $c_{u}c_{d}$ on two generic pairs.

\emph{Reading.} The action clause in its adjoint reading takes each family term to its adjoint; the action is the sum of each term and its adjoint for every $(Y, \tilde{Y})$, so the clause holds identically. The other statements of the Reading combine (i), (iii), (iv) with the stored exclusions named there.

check_py:
"""The phase of the quark mass determinant on the covariant completion: exact checks.

Family matrices are 3 x 3 with entries in span{1, I_4}, represented as Gaussian rationals (GA.QI; its unit stands
for I_4, and conj is I_4 -> -I_4). The stored completion: M_u = alpha Y + conj(beta) Yt, M_d = beta Y +
conj(alpha) Yt. Theta = det(M_u) det(M_d); H_q = M_q M_q^dagger; D = det[H_u, H_d].
(1) Off the balanced frame, |alpha| != |beta|, the map (Y, Yt) -> (M_u, M_d) is inverted by
    Y = (conj(alpha) M_u - conj(beta) M_d)/(|alpha|^2 - |beta|^2), Yt = (alpha M_d - beta M_u)/(|alpha|^2 - |beta|^2)
    and keeps symmetric pairs; turning M_u by a unit z keeps H_u, H_d and D and multiplies Theta by z^3. The
    hypercharge phase of the rung field leaves Theta, the common phase does not. On the balanced frame
    M_d = (beta/alpha) M_u and D = 0.
(2) Readings with a real Theta: real matrices (D = 0); the self-conjugate coupling Yt = conj(Y) in any frame
    (M_d = conj(M_u), Theta >= 0, D != 0, the two H have the same characteristic polynomial); Hermitian matrices
    in a real frame (Theta real, D != 0, different characteristic polynomials), which are real when symmetric.
(3) Stages: for X odd under the exchange of the first two families, with entries p, q, r, s,
    det(J + d (E + X)) = -3 d^2 x y + d^3 (q^2 - p^2), x y = (p - q - 2s)(p + q - 2r)/3 the product of the
    off-diagonal entries of the stored light-plane block; for a symmetric one-type stage X = t S it is
    -d^2 t^2 ((p - 2r)^2 + d p^2).
(4) One-type symmetric stages with real first stages: Theta = (c_u c_d)^3 (d_u d_d)^2 (t_u t_d)^2 R, R > 0. With
    the down coefficient real and the up coefficient at a quarter turn, Theta is real, of sign -sign(c_u c_d),
    with D != 0 and different spectra; the up matrix is fixed by conjugation composed with the family exchange and
    the down matrix by conjugation; at an eighth turn Theta is not real; a common conjugation of both gives D = 0.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F

import GA
from GA import QI
from tp_premise import premise

UNIT = QI(0, 1)


def mat(rows):
    return [[QI(x) for x in r] for r in rows]


def mm(A, B):
    return [[sum((A[r][m] * B[m][c] for m in range(len(B))), QI(0)) for c in range(len(B[0]))] for r in range(len(A))]


def madd(A, B, s=1):
    return [[a + QI(s) * b for a, b in zip(r, t)] for r, t in zip(A, B)]


def msc(c, A):
    return [[QI(c) * a for a in r] for r in A]


def conj(A):
    return [[a.conj() for a in r] for r in A]


def tr(A):
    return [list(r) for r in zip(*A)]


def dag(A):
    return tr(conj(A))


def det3(A):
    return (A[0][0] * (A[1][1] * A[2][2] - A[1][2] * A[2][1]) - A[0][1] * (A[1][0] * A[2][2] - A[1][2] * A[2][0])
            + A[0][2] * (A[1][0] * A[2][1] - A[1][1] * A[2][0]))


def herm_square(M):
    return mm(M, dag(M))


def big_d(Mu, Md):
    Hu, Hd = herm_square(Mu), herm_square(Md)
    return det3(madd(mm(Hu, Hd), mm(Hd, Hu), -1))


def charpoly(H):
    t1 = H[0][0] + H[1][1] + H[2][2]
    H2 = mm(H, H)
    t2 = H2[0][0] + H2[1][1] + H2[2][2]
    return (t1, (t1 * t1 - t2) / QI(2), det3(H))


def masses(al, be, Y, Yt):
    al, be = QI(al), QI(be)
    return madd(msc(al, Y), msc(be.conj(), Yt)), madd(msc(be, Y), msc(al.conj(), Yt))


def theta(Mu, Md):
    return det3(Mu) * det3(Md)


def is_real(z):
    return QI(z).im == 0


Y_S = mat([[QI(1, 2), QI(0, 1), 2], [QI(0, 1), 3, QI(1, -1)], [2, QI(1, -1), QI(5, 1)]])
YT_S = mat([[2, QI(1, 1), QI(0, 3)], [QI(1, 1), QI(-1, 2), 1], [QI(0, 3), 1, QI(4, -1)]])
JJ = mat([[1, 1, 1], [1, 1, 1], [1, 1, 1]])
EE = mat([[0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1]])
P12 = mat([[0, 1, 0], [1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1]])


def odd_stage(p, q, r, s):
    """The general matrix X with P12 X P12 = -X."""
    return mat([[p, q, r], [-QI(q), -QI(p), -QI(r)], [s, -QI(s), 0]])


def stage_matrix(c, d, X):
    return msc(c, madd(JJ, msc(d, madd(EE, X))))


def check_completion_is_a_bijection_off_the_balanced_frame():
    premise("synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix")
    premise("synthesis.imported-left-right-bidoublet-two-yukawa-couplings")
    ok = True
    for al, be in ((QI(F(1, 3)), QI(-3)), (QI(2, 1), QI(-1, 3))):
        Mu, Md = masses(al, be, Y_S, YT_S)
        m2 = al * al.conj() - be * be.conj()
        ok = ok and m2 != 0
        Yrec = msc(1 / m2, madd(msc(al.conj(), Mu), msc(be.conj(), Md), -1))
        Ytrec = msc(1 / m2, madd(msc(al, Md), msc(be, Mu), -1))
        ok = ok and Yrec == Y_S and Ytrec == YT_S
        # turn M_u by the unit z = (3 + 4 I_4)/5 and pull back
        z = QI(F(3, 5), F(4, 5))
        ok = ok and z * z.conj() == 1
        Yz = msc(1 / m2, madd(msc(al.conj(), msc(z, Mu)), msc(be.conj(), Md), -1))
        Ytz = msc(1 / m2, madd(msc(al, Md), msc(be, msc(z, Mu)), -1))
        Mu2, Md2 = masses(al, be, Yz, Ytz)
        ok = ok and Yz == tr(Yz) and Ytz == tr(Ytz) and Mu2 == msc(z, Mu) and Md2 == Md
        ok = ok and herm_square(Mu2) == herm_square(Mu) and big_d(Mu2, Md2) == big_d(Mu, Md)
        ok = ok and big_d(Mu, Md) != 0 and theta(Mu2, Md2) == z * z * z * theta(Mu, Md)
        ok = ok and z * z * z == QI(F(-117, 125), F(44, 125))
        # hypercharge phase and common phase of the rung field
        ok = ok and theta(*masses(z * al, z.conj() * be, Y_S, YT_S)) == theta(Mu, Md)
        ok = ok and theta(*masses(z * al, z * be, Y_S, YT_S)) != theta(Mu, Md)
    # balanced frame |alpha| = |beta|: 3^2 + 4^2 = 5^2
    al, be = QI(3, 4), QI(0, 5)
    Mu, Md = masses(al, be, Y_S, YT_S)
    ok = ok and al * al.conj() == be * be.conj() and Md == msc(be / al, Mu) and big_d(Mu, Md) == 0
    ok = ok and theta(Mu, Md) == (be / al) * (be / al) * (be / al) * det3(Mu) * det3(Mu)
    GA.check("completion: (Y, Yt) -> (M_u, M_d) invertible off the balanced frame; unit turn of M_u moves only det", ok)
    return ok


def check_readings_with_a_real_determinant():
    premise("synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix")

    Mu, Md = masses(al, be, Yr, msc(-1, Ytr))
    ok = ok and is_real(theta(Mu, Md)) and theta(Mu, Md).re < 0
    # (b) self-conjugate coupling, complex frame
    Mu, Md = masses(QI(2, 1), QI(-1, 3), Y_S, conj(Y_S))

    # Hermitian and symmetric is real: the Hermitian sample is not symmetric, its symmetric part is real
    sym = madd(Yh, tr(Yh))
    ok = ok and Yh != tr(Yh) and sym == conj(sym)
    GA.check("real determinant: real (D = 0); self-conjugate (equal spectra); Hermitian with a real frame", ok)

def check_stage_determinant_formula():
    premise("synthesis.solar-angle-light-plane-sum-rule")
    premise("synthesis.cabibbo-from-one-type-quark-stages-selects-near-quarter-turn-phase")
    ok = True
    samples = [(QI(2), QI(-1), QI(3), QI(5), QI(F(1, 7))), (QI(1, 2), QI(0, 1), QI(-2, 1), QI(3, -1), QI(F(2, 5))),
               (QI(0, 3), QI(4), QI(1, 1), QI(-2), QI(F(1, 3), 1))]
    for p, q, r, s, d in samples:
        X = odd_stage(p, q, r, s)
        ok = ok and mm(mm(P12, X), P12) == msc(-1, X)
        xy = (p - q - 2 * s) * (p + q - 2 * r) / 3
        # the light-plane block in the basis (1, 1, -2)/sqrt 6, (1, -1, 0)/sqrt 2: product of off-diagonal entries
        be_, bo_ = [QI(1), QI(1), QI(-2)], [QI(1), QI(-1), QI(0)]
        form = lambda u, w: sum((u[a] * X[a][b] * w[b] for a in range(3) for b in range(3)), QI(0))
        ok = ok and form(be_, bo_) * form(bo_, be_) / 12 == xy and form(be_, be_) == 0 and form(bo_, bo_) == 0
        ok = ok and sum((be_[a] * EE[a][b] * be_[b] for a in range(3) for b in range(3)), QI(0)) / 6 == QI(F(2, 3))
        lhs = det3(madd(JJ, msc(d, madd(EE, X))))
        ok = ok and lhs == -3 * d * d * xy + d * d * d * (q * q - p * p)
    # symmetric one-type stage X = t S, S real symmetric with entries p, r
    for p, r, t, d in ((QI(2), QI(-1), QI(1, 1), QI(F(1, 5))), (QI(3), QI(5), QI(0, 2), QI(F(2, 3)))):
        X = msc(t, odd_stage(p, 0, r, r))
        ok = ok and X == tr(X)
        ok = ok and det3(madd(JJ, msc(d, madd(EE, X)))) == -d * d * t * t * ((p - 2 * r) * (p - 2 * r) + d * p * p)
    GA.check("stages: det(J + d(E + X)) = -3 d^2 x y + d^3 (q^2 - p^2); one-type symmetric: -d^2 t^2 (positive)", ok)
    return ok


S_UP, S_DOWN = odd_stage(2, 0, -1, -1), odd_stage(1, 0, 3, 3)

def check_quarter_turn_stage_gives_a_real_determinant():
    premise("synthesis.cabibbo-from-one-type-quark-stages-selects-near-quarter-turn-phase")
    premise("synthesis.flag-conjugate-antilinear-on-one-chirality-and-conjugation-reverses-jarlskog")
    premise("synthesis.one-type-second-stages-are-twins")
    # down coefficient real, up coefficient a quarter turn: pinned values of the two determinants and of D
    Mu, Md = stage_pair(C_UP, C_DOWN, T_QUARTER, T_REAL)
    ok = Mu == tr(Mu) and Md == tr(Md)
    ok = ok and det3(Mu) == QI(F(115248, 125)) and det3(Md) == QI(F(-608, 3))
    ok = ok and theta(Mu, Md) == QI(F(-23356928, 125))
    ok = ok and big_d(Mu, Md) == QI(0, F(-149375920805085184, 1265625))
    ok = ok and charpoly(herm_square(Mu)) != charpoly(herm_square(Md))
    ok = ok and mm(mm(P12, conj(Mu)), P12) == Mu and conj(Md) == Md and mm(mm(P12, conj(Md)), P12) != Md
    # the Hermitian twin: M_u P12 is Hermitian, of opposite determinant
    tw = mm(Mu, P12)
    ok = ok and tw == dag(tw) and det3(tw) + det3(Mu) == 0
    # opposite sign of c_u c_d: the determinant is the opposite real number
    ok = ok and theta(*stage_pair(C_UP, -C_DOWN, T_QUARTER, T_REAL)) == QI(F(23356928, 125))
    # an eighth turn against a real coefficient: a quarter-turn determinant; opposite eighth turns: positive
    ok = ok and theta(*stage_pair(C_UP, C_DOWN, T_EIGHTH, T_REAL)) == QI(0, F(11678464, 125))
    ok = ok and theta(*stage_pair(C_UP, C_DOWN, T_EIGHTH, T_EIGHTH_BAR)) == QI(F(23356928, 125))
    ok = ok and big_d(*stage_pair(C_UP, C_DOWN, T_EIGHTH, T_EIGHTH_BAR)) != 0
    # general law: Theta / (t_u t_d)^2 is real, with the sign of c_u c_d
    for tu, td in GENERIC:
        ratio = theta(*stage_pair(C_UP, C_DOWN, tu, td)) / (tu * tu * td * td)
        ok = ok and is_real(ratio) and ratio.re > 0
        ratio = theta(*stage_pair(-C_UP, C_DOWN, tu, td)) / (tu * tu * td * td)
        ok = ok and is_real(ratio) and ratio.re < 0
    # a common conjugation of both sectors (both coefficients real, or both quarter turns) gives D = 0
    ok = ok and big_d(*stage_pair(C_UP, C_DOWN, T_REAL, T_REAL)) == 0
    ok = ok and big_d(*stage_pair(C_UP, C_DOWN, T_QUARTER, UNIT * T_REAL)) == 0
    # cos(2 phi) = 2 cos^2 phi - 1 equals -1/2 at cos^2 phi = 1/4 and -1 at the quarter turn
    ok = ok and 2 * F(1, 4) - 1 == F(-1, 2) and 2 * F(0, 4) - 1 == -1
    GA.check("quarter turn in one sector, real vacuum: det real with D != 0 and different spectra; sign -sign(c_u c_d)", ok)
    return ok
